Convex lens — from upload to simulation

Actual input · expected input · actual output · expected output · error propagation

Trace: TRACE-LENS-20261016-001-NATIVE-RETRY-20261017

Trace ID: `TRACE-LENS-20261016-001-NATIVE-RETRY-20261017`. These documents use the existing live native Windows request from 2026-10-17. No models, detectors or solvers were rerun while writing them. No production fixes were made. Source reference: A convex lens, horizontal principal axis, upright object to the left between F and 2F, inverted enlarged image to the right beyond 2F, focal markers and principal rays. Printed f=15 cm. Known and unknown evidence: 15 cm is OCR-groundable focal length. Object/lens/image/ray positions and F spacing must be measured from the source. The drawing suggests the between-F-and-2F image-formation case; no exact object distance or annotated pixel coordinates are supplied. Expected geometry for this diagram: Ground the whole lens/axis, object base and tip, image base and tip, focal markers and ray paths independently. A missing object detection must remain missing evidence, not become an assumed exploration object. Expected initial simulation: At t=0 the object should occupy its printed arrow and the image/rays should be compared to the printed image/rays. The actual solver returns real_same_size from assumed u=2f, whereas the source depicts an enlarged image. This demonstrates an input/model mismatch, not an arithmetic failure. Exact expected coordinates/masks are unavailable: EXPECTED ARTIFACT NOT AVAILABLE — NO GROUND TRUTH EXISTS. Expected behavior below is a contract or a qualitative source comparison, never a hand-drawn expected result.

Markdown document · Original forensic call index

How to use this document

Read stages 01–34 in order. Blue panels show recorded data; green panels show expected contracts and source-specific requirements. Full snapshots are expandable. Mutation output is distinguished from a None/undefined function return. Earlier startup/demo events are excluded. A structural pass does not certify visual registration.

“NOT EXECUTED” means the branch did not run. “Not separately captured” means an internal operation was reached but its own call arguments were not intercepted. No expected pixels or runtime outputs have been invented.

Expected output

Satisfied/missing requirements, issues, blockers and warnings consistent with available evidence. Visual correctness and mere field presence must be evaluated separately.

For this diagram

15 cm is OCR-groundable focal length. Object/lens/image/ray positions and F spacing must be measured from the source. The drawing suggests the between-F-and-2F image-formation case; no exact object distance or annotated pixel coordinates are supplied.

What changed and what may have been lost

The current analyzer checks required entities/parameters and ambiguity. It does not compare every proposed line or point to image pixels.

Domain scene objects, parameters and geometry that preserve evidence/provenance and source frame. If model geometry is reconstructed, distinguish it from observed geometry.

Expected output

A response whose status, scene, BookIR and readiness agree, correlated to this source and trace. HTTP 200 does not itself mean a simulation is ready.

For this diagram

15 cm is OCR-groundable focal length. Object/lens/image/ray positions and F spacing must be measured from the source. The drawing suggests the between-F-and-2F image-formation case; no exact object distance or annotated pixel coordinates are supplied.

What changed and what may have been lost

This is the handler return, after nested work. Exact HTTP status/body are retained separately from the Python object.

Expected output

Invertible mapping with the same image/overlay scale and offsets. Applying viewToSource(sourceToView(p)) should recover the supplied point within floating-point precision.

For this diagram

15 cm is OCR-groundable focal length. Object/lens/image/ray positions and F spacing must be measured from the source. The drawing suggests the between-F-and-2F image-formation case; no exact object distance or annotated pixel coordinates are supplied.

What changed and what may have been lost

sourceToView includes viewport letterboxing; sourceToOverlay omits it because the overlay is already image-aligned. Browser coordinates add the measured image origin. Do not add letterboxing twice.

Expected output

Motion evolves runtime state only; reset restores initial compiled values. Exact 0.5 s / 1 s states cannot be asserted unless their saved timestamps say so.

For this diagram

At t=0 the object should occupy its printed arrow and the image/rays should be compared to the printed image/rays. The actual solver returns real_same_size from assumed u=2f, whereas the source depicts an enlarged image. This demonstrates an input/model mismatch, not an arithmetic failure.

What changed and what may have been lost

The executed main.js path automatically starts after a successful load. Later frames are saved at their actual times. Optics results are static ray solutions rather than pendulum-like time evolution.

Complete handoff JSON

Runtime subcomponents and capture boundary

These internal components are distinguished explicitly so a saved outer runtime result is not mistaken for six separate function traces.

ComponentExpected inputExpected outputActual evidence / gap
validatePhysicsSceneNormalized canonical sceneValidation result / typed issuesNot separately intercepted; successful load shows continuation, not a saved validation-result object.
SimulationCapabilityRegistry.resolveValidated normalized sceneInteractive scene/capabilitiesNo separate before/after capture. Use PhysicsRuntime source and actual runtime boundary; do not assume its output equals its input.
SolverRegistry.resolveInteractive sceneMatching domain adapterNo separately serialized adapter return. Runtime domain/output and the executed load path establish the adapter route.
Adapter.initializeInteractive scene, container and optionsInitialized adapter stateInitial runtime output/state is captured, but this child call’s exact argument object is not separately recorded.
Domain solverAdapter-derived model argumentsPhysics solution/stateActual solution/state is captured. Exact internal solver-call arguments are not a separate artifact.
Renderer.render / PendulumSimulation.renderRuntime solution/state and mapperSVG/canvas outputActual SVG/canvas and DOM measurements are captured; per-draw-call arguments are not.

Appendix B. First failure and propagation

Last known good: Source identity, semantic subtype and selected OCR focal-length text (15 cm).

First suspicious: Secondary OCR misreads the focal label; router retains the correct RapidOCR result. The Object OCR box (188,220,135,57) is valid text evidence, but its four-pixel expansion reaches adjacent ray geometry.

First definitive failure: OCR edge masking erases part of the incident ray beside the Object label; CV subsequently omits the printed object arrow and selects a partial lens centerline.

Downstream chain: Grounder retains the center/partial aperture and observes focal_length=0.15 m from OCR, but does not ground the object or printed focal-marker spacing. _normalize_lens_focal_length substitutes aperture×0.5=117 px as focal length. _normalize_lens_exploration_object supplies objectDistance=234 px and objectHeight=81.9 px despite the semantic object already being present in the source. These are auto_policy assumptions, not observed placements. No user accepted them during this trace. Compiler carries lens_center=(641,432), f=117, u=234 into the scene and normalizes objectHeight to −81.9 in source Y-down coordinates. Runtime object base=(407,432), tip=(407,350.1); image is x=875, height=81.9. Model output is consistent with the substituted parameters, not registered to the original object/rays.

Separation of failure classes: preprocessing/perception is demonstrated upstream; a shared coordinate conversion error is not demonstrated; numerical solver failure is not established. The circuit never reaches a solver.

Appendix C. Capture limits

No new run was performed. The recorder captured repository Python boundaries and GenAI model calls, not private neural-library/C internals. JS boundary events, normalized scenes, actual solver outputs and DOM captures exist; separate entry/exit snapshots for every registry/adapter/renderer child function do not. These gaps are labeled, not filled with reconstructed output. Several void JS returns appear as captureError because undefined is not JSON; resulting state is separately recorded. Two class-serialization errors exist in the historical recorder log; integrity verification found the required snapshot files present for every indexed call. No exact expected pixel dataset, mask or numerical physical state has been authored.
